numerical_failure.observed_behavior: scipy.special.hyperu(a,1,x) gives output values that are extremely off (by several magnitudes) for x close to 0 when a is close to 0 and b=1; e.g. errors appear near x=0.01 for a=0.1. No error message is raised, just a miscalculation.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Values should agree with mpmath.hyperu at the reference values; the test asserts agreement with mpmath reference values at rtol=1e-13 for b == 1, |a| < 0.25, 0 < x < 1. The fix uses DLMF 13.3.7 in that region.
trigger_conditions: a close to 0 (|a| < 0.25 in the regression test region)
x close to 0 (0 < x < 1, errors appear e.g. near x=0.01 with a=0.1)

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: small x (about 1e-5 to 0.1 in the regression test, near x=0.01 in the issue report) with small |a| (|a| < 0.25 in the test region; -0.25 < a < 0.3 in the patch condition)
category_specific_evidence: Issue #15650 reports scipy.special.hyperu(a,b,x) giving values off by several magnitudes for a close to 0, b=1, and x close to 0, with no error message, only a miscalculation.
The issue reporter saw no such errors for |a| > 0.5, so the discrepancy is confined to small |a|.
The reviewed patch in _hypergeometric.pxd applies DLMF 13.3.7 only when b == 1 and x < 1 and -0.25 < a < 0.3.
The regression test test_gh_15650_mp uses mpmath reference values at 100 digits, with a drawn from uniform(-0.25, 0.25) and x from logspace(-5, -1, 4), compared at rtol=1e-13.
A later discussion proposes an alternative guard of b == 1 and abs(a) < 1 and abs(x) < 1, and says the threshold was chosen more carefully.
The PR title is 'Fix hyperu for b = 1, small x, small a'.
reproduction_risks: The passages give different region guards (-0.25 < a < 0.3 in the pxd diff versus abs(a) < 1 and abs(x) < 1 in a discussion snippet), so the exact trigger region is not settled.
The reference values come from mpmath at 100 digits; a reproduction must use high-precision mpmath values as expected output, not double-precision output.
The dtype the discrepancy depends on is not stated in the passages; the input/output examples only label values as float.
The magnitude at which errors appear is only approximate (near x=0.01 with a=0.1 in the issue).
The scipy version under test is not stated in the passages, so the buggy commit cannot be confirmed from them.
